questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word: APOGEE
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. **Pinnacle**.

__
 
• The word **“apogee”** means the highest point in the development of something; the climax or culmination. (पराकाष्ठा / शिखर)

 
 
• **Example:** The singer reached the apogee of her career after winning the international award.
 
 
 
• **“Pinnacle”** refers to the most successful point, the peak, or the highest level of achievement. (शिखर)
 
 
• **Example:** Reaching the pinnacle of the corporate ladder takes years of dedication and hard work.
 
 
 
• Therefore, the word “pinnacle” is the most appropriate synonym for “apogee.”

Therefore, the correct answer is- Pinnacle

• **Example:** The height of Mount Everest makes it the tallest mountain in the world.
 
 
 
• **Valley** (घाटी): A low area of land between hills or mountains.
 
 
• **Example:** The river flows through a beautiful valley surrounded by mountains.
 
 
 
• **Foot** (पैर / तल): The lowest part or bottom of something.
 
 
• **Example:** The village is located at the foot of the hill.

questions.question: Select the correct option: The journalist refused to ___ her confidential notes.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**give up**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrasal verb "**give up**" in this context means to surrender or hand over possession of something, usually under pressure or demand.
 
• The sentence describes a situation where a journalist is protecting her sources, meaning she would refuse to surrender or "**give up**" her notes to authorities.
 
• **Options 1, 2**, and **3** do not convey the correct meaning in this specific context.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"The journalist refused to **give up**__ her confidential notes."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "give out"** is incorrect because it means to distribute something to many people or to stop functioning.
 
• **Option 2: "give over"** is incorrect because while it can mean to hand something over, it is less commonly used in modern English for surrendering items under pressure.
 
• **Option 3: "give away"** is incorrect because it means to accidentally reveal a secret or to give something away for free as a gift.

questions.question: Select the correct option: Her proposal was completely and fundamentally ____ to existing theories.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**contrary**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct word to use is "**contrary**." The phrase "contrary to" means in opposition to or inconsistent with, which fits the context of the sentence.
 
• "Contrary to existing theories" is a standard and idiomatic expression in academic and formal writing.
 
• **Options 2, 3**, and 4 do not form the correct or most natural phrase in this context.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"Her proposal was completely and fundamentally **contrary**__ to existing theories."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "contrasting"** is incorrect; while it means showing differences, it is not the standard collocation with "to" in this context.
 
• **Option 3: "opposite"** does not fit the formal construction here ("opposite to" is less common and less precise).
 
• **Option 4: "adverse"** means harmful or unfavorable, not suitable for this context.

questions.question: Find the part containing an error:The committee’s recommendations, extensive in detail (1)/ triggered debate not only within the ministry (2)/ but also among analysts who claim they (3)/ lacked prior access to essential reports. (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is a tense inconsistency between the verbs "claim" and "lacked."
 
• The verb "claim" is in the present tense, while "lacked" is in the past tense, which creates a mismatch.
 
• To maintain consistency, both verbs should be in the same tense.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part 3** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The committee’s recommendations, extensive in detail, triggered debate not only within the ministry but also among analysts who **claimed they lacked** prior access to essential reports."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1: "The committee’s recommendations, extensive in detail"** – This part is grammatically correct and sets the context.
 
• **2: "triggered debate not only within the ministry"** – This part is correct and uses appropriate structure.
 
• **4: "lacked prior access to essential reports."** – This part is correct and uses appropriate structure.

questions.question: Change the sentence from active to passive:“The panel has drafted a final proposal.”

options.text: A final proposal has been drafted by the panel.
A final proposal was being drafted by the panel.
A final proposal had been drafted by the panel.
A final proposal is drafted by the panel.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "The panel has drafted a final proposal."
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "a final proposal" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "has drafted" to "has been drafted" (present perfect passive).
 
• Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "the panel."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"A final proposal has been drafted by the panel."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: **"A final proposal was being drafted by the panel." – Incorrect tense (past continuous passive).
 
• **Option 3: **"A final proposal had been drafted by the panel." – Incorrect tense (past perfect passive).
 
• **Option 4: **"A final proposal is drafted by the panel." – Incorrect tense (simple present passive).

questions.question: Convert from passive to active:“The documents are believed to have been leaked by insiders.”

options.text: It is believed that insiders leaked the documents.
The insiders are believed to have leaked the documents.
The leak allegedly exposed the documents.

questions.solution:

__
 
• Active voice structure: The subject of the passive voice sentence becomes the agent or doer of the action in the active voice.
 
• In the passive voice, the sentence is: "The documents are believed to have been leaked by insiders."
 
• To convert to active voice: Place the agent "the insiders" at the beginning.
 
• Use the structure "are believed to have leaked" for the active construction.
 
• This maintains the same meaning as the original sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The insiders are believed to have leaked the documents."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Option 2: **"Insiders allegedly leaked the documents." – The word "allegedly" is not in the original sentence and changes the nuance.
 
• **Option 4: **"The leak allegedly exposed the documents." – This changes both the subject and the meaning.

questions.question: Convert to indirect speech:She said, “I had completed the report.”

options.text: She said she completed the report.
She said she has completed the report.
She said that she had completed the report.
She said she had been completing the report.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** She said that she had completed the report.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• The reporting verb "said" is followed by "that" when converting to indirect speech.
 
• The pronoun "I" changes to "she" to match the subject.
 
• The past perfect tense ("had completed") remains unchanged in indirect speech as the reporting verb is in the past.
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Quotation marks are removed in indirect speech.
 
• Sentence structure is adjusted to a statement, not a direct quote.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *She said that she had completed the report.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** She said she completed the report. 

 
 
• Incorrect tense; does not convey the past perfect meaning.
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** She said she has completed the report. 
 
 
• Incorrect tense; present perfect is not appropriate here.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** She said she had been completing the report. 
 
 
• Incorrect tense; this is past perfect continuous and changes the meaning.

questions.question:
Rearrange the sentences into a coherent paragraph:

1. This ensures survival of the best-adapted individuals.

2. Life’s diversity has arisen over long periods.

3. Useful traits accumulate gradually.

4. Variation grants some individuals an advantage.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The paragraph discusses the process of evolution and how diversity in life has developed over time.
 
• **Sentence 2 is the first sentence** as it introduces the overarching idea of life’s diversity evolving over time:
 
 
• "Life’s diversity has arisen over long periods."
 
 
 
• **Sentence 4 follows** by explaining how variation plays a role in evolution:
 
 
• "Variation grants some individuals an advantage."
 
 
 
• **Sentence 3 is next** as it describes how these advantageous traits accumulate:
 
 
• "Useful traits accumulate gradually."
 
 
 
• **Sentence 1 concludes** by stating the result of this process:
 
 
• "This ensures survival of the best-adapted individuals."
 
 
 
• The correct sequence is **2, 4, 3, 1**.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

"Life’s diversity has arisen over long periods. Variation grants some individuals an advantage. Useful traits accumulate gradually. This ensures survival of the best-adapted individuals."
